name: Port Wine Cellars of Gaia
short: The port wine lodges, or 'caves', of Vila Nova de Gaia, where port has been aged for centuries; home to Croft, Taylor's, Sandeman, Graham's and Ramos Pinto.
long: Vila Nova de Gaia, on the south bank of the Douro, is the historic centre of port wine ageing. The grapes are grown in the Upper Douro valley, and the wine has long been carried downriver to Gaia, where it matures in the cool, damp cellars the locals call 'caves'. history:
Vila Nova de Gaia, on the south bank of the Douro, is the historic centre of port wine ageing. The grapes are grown in the Upper Douro valley, and the wine has long been carried downriver to Gaia, where it matures in the cool, damp cellars the locals call 'caves', from the Portuguese word for cellars.

The move to Gaia was driven by climate: the mouth of the Douro is cooler and damper than the hot wine-growing valley, and the proximity of Porto and the Atlantic made export easier. In 1777, after the reforms of the Douro Wine Company, Gaia became the official storage and ageing site for all exported port.

The oldest trading houses settled here in the 17th to 19th centuries: Croft (1678), Taylor's (1692), Sandeman (1790), Cockburn's (1815), Graham's (1820) and Ramos Pinto (1880). Long stone warehouses lined with oak casks and bottle cellars grew up along the Avenida Diogo Leite.

Port is a fortified wine: grape spirit is added during fermentation to stop it and preserve the sweetness. Today most lodges are open for tours and tastings, and the Gaia waterfront has become one of the city's main tourist routes.
facts: Port has been aged in Gaia since the 18th century; in 1777 the town became the official storage site for exported wine.
The name 'caves' comes from the Portuguese word for cellars.
Among the oldest houses: Croft (1678), Taylor's (1692), Sandeman (1790), Graham's (1820), Ramos Pinto (1880).
The cool, damp climate at the mouth of the Douro makes Gaia ideal for ageing fortified wine.
Port is a fortified wine: spirit is added to the must to stop fermentation and keep the sweetness.
tip: Book a tour with tasting in advance, especially in summer: Sandeman, Taylor's and Ramos Pinto can have queues. You can walk here across the lower deck of the Dom Luís I Bridge or take the Gaia cable car.
